api_safety.backward_compatibility: New extension type. Previously -urur-/-oror- surfaces were mislabeled as reversive style long; they now analyze and generate as repetitive. Clients requesting reversive style long_urur/urur/oror receive a 422 pointing at this type.

counterexamples.note: Labeling -oror- as reversive was the pre-v3 implementation bug; reversive on an o-radical is -onor- (see reversive card).

examples.note: Source radical -rond-oror- (track thoroughly) from -rond- (track); o-radicals take -oror-.

notes: Repetitive (-urur- / -oror-) is a distinct extension from reversive with its own meaning; the two must never share a semantic label.
Finite forms (e.g. ndinokororora) are constructed combinations of these attested radicals with the supported present construction.
The type takes no style argument; any style value returns 422.

qa.reviewer_notes: Radical triples verified by visual inspection of the local PDF page, paragraphs (a) and (b). Separated from reversive, which it was previously conflated with.

rule_summary: Repetitive extension -urur- (default, including after /e/ and on C radicals) and -oror- after radical /o/.
source_locator: Fortune, Shona Grammatical Constructions Vol. 1 (1985), section 2.10.2.3.3 'Extended radicals', PDF p. 33 (printed p. 21), paragraphs (a) and (b)
title: Repetitive extension distinct from reversive
